what: The Streamlit front end was replaced by a plain HTML page, served by a small Python server on your own machine.
The page follows design.pdf: each watchlist opens on its Needs review queue, and a trial page shows previous and new values side by side.
All trials, New matches and Summary are tabs of one watchlist. Find trials has its own screen. Renaming, deleting and adding are small dialogs.
Streamlit, the in-browser runtime and the GitHub Pages site were deleted.
It was built as the feature's tickets, then a whole-branch review and a round of fix tickets. All of it is on main, in pull request #1.
so_what: The analyst sees what changed before opening anything, and can review it without losing their place.
A trial that could not be checked, a saved search that failed and a registry that could not be reached are each said in words. Nothing that failed is shown as current.
One failure is not in words: with the local server stopped, an action shows the browser's own "Failed to fetch". It is among the findings left as they are.
It runs on your machine only, on a desktop: designed at 1440 pixels wide, working down to 1024. Phones were ruled out in the brief.
The tickets alone did not catch everything: walkers and the review found defects after the tickets were done, and the re-check found more.
now_what: Nothing waits on a decision about the build. It is merged, and you signed off its run-through on 11 November 2026.
This page was made afterwards, so that you can judge the page itself.
The recording was made on today's code, not on the commit the build ended at. The page says which commit.
The checks run log did not exist during this build, so the page cannot say how many check runs were red.
The findings here are not every finding: 37 come from the old defect log and nine from the spec's list of walker findings not fixed.
The review recorded 62. Its 17 blocking ones are here; the other 45 are accounted for in .scratch/pr-1-review/ranked.md. Seven more from its second read are not here.
No severity was recorded for any finding. One walker row can stand for several things the walkers reported, because the old log merged them.
Many findings read "fixed, no check named": the old log names the walk that shows the fix for the re-check findings only.
The review's 17 fates rest on its second read, which says each fix landed (.scratch/pr-1-review/findings/round-1.md). It names a test or walk for six of them.
One of the 17 landed with a gap: a check still checked a trial removed while it ran. Fix ticket 18 closed it.
The fix round left an Open list of 22 items, accepted at sign-off because no objection was raised. Only item 6 is on this page; the rest are in .scratch/pr-1-review/spec.md.
